paper.title: MobileAgent: enhancing mobile control via human-machine interaction and SOP integration
paper.central_claim: Integrating human-machine structured interaction and SOP task-pipeline/completion-state information enhances mobile automation and instruction prediction, including66.92% AitW performance, while maintaining inference cost; privacy-sensitive choices are returned to users.

evidence.quote: it is challenging for agents to establish a relationship between current page operations and task objectives from fragmented and redundant user operational behaviors.
evidence.support_explanation: Original problem: noisy/variable trajectories obscure essential task pipeline.

evidence.quote: some privacy-related decisions cannot be fully automated, as they necessitate user awareness and confirmation.
evidence.support_explanation: Original privacy/personalization objective needs user awareness and confirmation, not unconditional autonomy.

evidence.quote: we employ ’Enlarged-element’ operations, which map coordinates to specific page elements by expanding each element’s coordinate bounding box.
evidence.support_explanation: Enlarged-element preprocessing predicts element targets instead of raw click coordinates, with fixed-direction scroll mapping.

evidence.quote: For application pages that require user awareness and authorization, the agent is designed to accurately identify and enable the production of well-structured messages and user operation choices. This empowers users to select operations themselves, effectively replacing the model’s direct execution of commands.
evidence.support_explanation: Structured instructions replace direct execution with user-presented information/options.

evidence.quote: SOPs function as a blueprint for the model’s instruction execution pipeline on the input side, while a plan dictates future action strategies during the output phase.
evidence.support_explanation: Author explicitly attributes prior SOP use to MetaGPT; this paper moves abstract workflow/state to mobile input conditioning.

evidence.quote: | H ⁡ ( Y | X , Z ) ≤ H ⁡ ( Y | X ) H(Y|X,Z)\leq H(Y|X) |
evidence.support_explanation: Conditional entropy inequality is generic; it does not establish availability of useful SOP at deployment.

evidence.quote: The AIA is a product currently in the testing and development phase, not yet released for public use, designed and developed for dialogue scenarios where large models generate instructions to aid user automation in mobile applications.
evidence.support_explanation: Task goals/history/DOM input and three output categories; product still in development.

evidence.quote: the AI agent generates structured notification content and user-required confirmation options, such as ’I understand’.
evidence.support_explanation: Concrete notification extraction and confirmation example, not a measured privacy-safety endpoint.

evidence.quote: We have delineated 13 fundamental SOP sub-tasks within the medical in-context
evidence.support_explanation: AIA SOP labels come from13 hand-defined subtask classes and a BERT click-text classifier.

evidence.quote: Task completion rate is utilized as a metric to evaluate the effectiveness of predictions. Initially, a partial score is determined by dividing the number of correct actions by the episode length. Subsequently, the task completion score is computed as the average of all partial scores.
evidence.support_explanation: Metric called task completion is mean correct-action fraction, not binary executed task completion.

evidence.quote: we collected corresponding tasks from 38 hospital applications, amassing a total of approximately 20,000 episodes. Of these, around 2,000 episodes were allocated for testing purposes.
evidence.support_explanation: Private medical data provenance,approx20k episodes/~2k test, Qwen7B LoRA; no app-heldout partition specified.

signatures.object: Mobile action representation and element association
signatures.information: Goal, role, previous actions and DOM/OCR/icon-derived element descriptors. Training uses demonstration click coordinates.
signatures.operation: Expand element bounding boxes to associate clicks with elements; output symbolic element target/type rather than raw coordinates; swipes mapped to direction and predetermined distance.
signatures.output: Executable action/element or typed text; structured environment index
signatures.conditions: Correct element extraction, unique assignment after expansion, known scroll geometry
signatures.feedback: Offline reference action; observed current screen in proposed runtime loop
signatures.selection_rule: Predefined action/element conversion, not candidate proposal acceptance learning
signatures.persistence: Fixed preprocessing and LoRA policy weights; no self-selected cross-task retained update.
signatures.later_use: Trained policy deployed on subsequent inputs; no online skill bank.
signatures.claimed_effect: Simplify relationship between page elements and predicted actions.
signatures.failure_boundary: OCR/icon misses and ambiguous/overlapping elements; no separate mapping ablation.

signatures.object: SOP-conditioned mobile policy training and task-state input
signatures.information: Task/history/DOM plus abstract SOP and finish/unfinish states in examples. SOP derived from action sequences; future unfinished tasks can appear. Prediction original-prompt versus SOP-present descriptions unresolved.
signatures.operation: Map medical click text via13class BERT or AitW hand rules to subtasks, drop back/close/Others, merge sequence, add state; mix SOP-augmented with original samples in LoRA training.
signatures.output: Short action prediction instead of outputting complete plan/state
signatures.conditions: Task pipeline and current completion state must be available without test-reference/future-action privilege or must transfer through training-only augmentation; paper does not settle exact regime.
signatures.feedback: Demonstration labels and SFT loss, not online task outcome reward
signatures.selection_rule: Hand-defined category/rule abstraction; model fitted to samples; no explicit accepted/rejected policy update loop.
signatures.selection_data: Private~20k episodes or AitW; GoogleApps10% train sampling, others full. Mixing ratio and independence not identified.
signatures.persistence: SFT LoRA parameters and fixed category rules; in-task completion state. No empirically selected retained self-improver.
signatures.later_use: Inference claimed original prompt/no longer response; exact inference SOP/state provenance unknown.
signatures.claimed_effect: AitW macro action-fraction65.43→66.92 with same21-token/.071s reported response.
signatures.failure_boundary: Schema availability mismatch, removing failure/recovery actions, instruction-overlap and cost accounting; entropy inequality insufficient.

signatures.information: Current app DOM fragments; task/history and trained medical interaction examples
signatures.operation: Recognize permission/notification/slot-choice pages and extract structured information/options for human choice instead of direct action.
signatures.output: Operational, task-status or structured user-interaction instruction
signatures.conditions: Reliable trigger, faithful extraction, explicit user response and enforcement before action; exact full schema missing from supplied panels.
signatures.feedback: Human selection conceptually changes task path; only offline instruction correctness measured.
signatures.selection_rule: Model predicts interaction category/options; ask timing calibration, refusal policy and deterministic execution gate not established.
signatures.selection_data: Qwen7B medical training;~2k test episodes total, no structured subset denominator.
signatures.persistence: Fixed trained policy; user-specific transient input, no lasting permission memory reported.
signatures.later_use: Current task continues after user choice; no measured later-task learning.
signatures.claimed_effect: Respect user awareness/privacy and improve structured prediction .460→.606.
signatures.failure_boundary: No privacy-violation/false-consent rates, ask burden, overasking/underasking or online completion comparison.

gap.author_gap: Arbitrary/redundant mobile trajectories obscure a consistent subtask pipeline; sensitive choices require user confirmation; output plans increase online generation cost.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete workflow/permission examples make the application problem credible. Same-backbone output-plan controls score lower than baseline; SOP arm is1.49pp above base on an offline action-fraction metric. Input-side useful SOP/state is the load-bearing unresolved premise.

lineage.relationship: Acknowledged SOP ancestor; current source uses role-sequenced workflow and structured inter-agent artifacts, unlike mobile input-side SOP training.
lineage.historical_limit: Do not treat v7-specific details as independently verified Jan2024 prior-art facts.

lineage.relationship: Earlier planning/history/reason-action interleaving; does not establish this SOP augmentation or human-authorization method.

lineage.version: Only target-paper author-cited; no fixed independent original supplied
lineage.relationship: Direct mobile policy comparators acknowledged in target; frontier comparison unresolved.

gap.closest_adjacent: Prior mobile instruction-conditioned policies and output plan/state generation; SOP workflow reuse is explicitly acknowledged, not newly invented in general.
gap.residue: Specific mobile element/action conversion, training-time pipeline/state conditioning with short action outputs, and structured medical authorization interaction.
gap.stakes: Wrong sensitive actions harm users; additional output plans may slow automation and variable trajectories complicate prediction.
gap.method_response: Replace raw click geometry with element outputs; abstract trajectories into SOP/state inputs; train mixed samples; return sensitive choices to user.
gap.remaining_gap: Exact deployment-time SOP/state acquisition, instruction/app holdout, actual privacy benefit, whole-task execution success, robust user-interaction triggers and full latency.

claims.text: SOP improves AIA medical operation, task-status and structured instruction prediction.
claims.setting: Qwen7B LoRA;38 hospital apps/~20k episodes,~2k heldout test; Chinese private contractor data.
claims.selection_vs_test: Episode split only; app/instruction and SOP-classifier construction separation unspecified.
claims.denominator: ~2000 private test episodes in total; category counts, exact splits and variance not supplied.
claims.budget: SFT with LoRA; precise Qwen training/data-mixing matching and full user burden not reported.
counterevidence: Metric is action-fraction score; does not measure privacy leakage, correct consent or completed user tasks.
No human interaction timing/effort or deterministic permission-gate audit.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Reported offline prediction-score gains in this private medical dataset; not quantified privacy safety or online task success.

claims.text: SOP improves overall AitW performance to66.92% without longer response generation.
claims.setting: Llama2 LoRA; episode-wise split across five AitW subsets;GoogleApps10% training sample;8A100,5epochs,5e-5.
claims.selection_vs_test: SOP derived from demonstrations; test-time pipeline/state source and mixing ratio unresolved. Table2 is full dataset totals, not evaluated test denominator.
claims.denominator: Unreported exact evaluated AitW episodes/steps per arm; equal macro average across five subsets.
claims.budget: Common stated hardware/epochs and short output, but sample mixing/equal information not settled.
counterevidence: Future unfinished sequence visible in example and input-side descriptions versus original-prompt inference: ambiguity, not proven label leakage.
No task/app-disjoint holdout or online success.
Overall66.92 is final score, not66.92% improvement.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported1.49pp offline macro prediction-score gain for this experimental recipe; full causal deployment mechanism unresolved.

claims.text: Inference cost unchanged, and10x faster than output plan+state.
claims.setting: vLLM,float16,max128 response tokens; inference seconds/number predictions.
claims.selection_vs_test: Timing dataset, batch/concurrency, input lengths, repeats and SOP-generation/preprocessing accounting unspecified.
claims.denominator: Number of inference calls n not specified; response length only.
claims.budget: Same named serving framework and precision; not full end-to-end cost.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Reported response-only time and length equal baseline in Table5;10x assertion contradicted, practical no-additional-cost claim scoped to reported prediction timing.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Tables support author-reported offline instruction/action-fraction gains: AitW65.43→66.92 macro (+1.49pp), medical structured .460→.606; Table5 reports .071s and21 response tokens, equal to base. They do not establish whole-task mobile success or privacy safety. Central SOP inference-information availability is unresolved, while the explicit10x speed assertion is contradicted by its own table.
unresolved: Are exact SOP and finish/unfinish states present during evaluated prediction, only privileged training augmentation, or generated using deployable information? How are they constructed for an unseen task without reference future actions?
Exact AitW test denominator, mixing ratio, app/instruction partition, label-classifier construction isolation, seeds/uncertainty and independent failure audit.
Full appendix Figure5 instruction schema panel missing from supplied figures; textual categories and notification example suffice for partial interface judgment, not an exact complete schema claim.
Auto-UI/BC direct original comparisons unavailable; no exhaustive novelty verdict.
assessment.replication_status: author_report_only; no model training, collected code execution or environment experiment performed
assessment.retained_assessment: Static preprocessing and supervised LoRA weights, not a self-selected or demonstrated retained improvement loop.
assessment.rubric_warning: Independent provisional assessment against fixed draft_uncalibrated v2.2. Known limitations justify finite lower tiers; unresolved inference detail is not assigned a fabricated value.

G.reason: Noisy histories, human authorization and inference overhead are real mobile-control concerns with concrete examples. SOP/planning/history ancestors acknowledged; direct Auto-UI/BC frontier comparison remains author-cited rather than independently checked, and generic entropy reduction is not a specific demonstrated residual bottleneck.

M.reason: Concrete element-index preprocessing, user-facing structured outputs and SOP+state training define testable changes; matched Llama2 plan/state controls are useful. Useful input SOP availability and how it avoids future-label privilege at deployment are ambiguous; entropy inequality does not resolve that prerequisite.

X.reason: Main transformations, training arms, hand-defined mappings and output categories can be followed. Full schema panel is absent from materials and test-time SOP/state generation remains unclear; no formal stopping/permission gate enforcement or recovery protocol demonstrated. This is partial execution clarity, not an invented retained loop.

E.measurement.reason: Tables show prediction gains under an explicitly defined action-fraction score, not whole-task success. Structured output accuracy is relevant but privacy protection, consent correctness and real task outcomes are not measured; response speed contradicts its10x prose.

E.causality.reason: Four same-backbone training arms constrain one alternative explanation, but SOP mixed-example counts/input privilege and deployment availability are unresolved; enlarged-element and interaction modules lack isolated controls. Cross-LLM results mix modality and training data.

E.holdout.reason: Episode-wise AitW holdout and~2k private test episodes provide some heldout observations. No unseen-instruction/app/site isolation, BERT/SOP-label construction isolation or reference-trajectory privilege audit; uncertainty is not proof of leakage.

E.statistics.reason: Five-subset averages and approximate private test count available; exact per-arm AitW test denominator, instruction-category counts, seed variation, intervals and systematic failure audit not found. A1.49pp gain lacks variance characterization.
search_scope: Dataset totals Table2 are not evaluated test denominators

E.cost.reason: Shared vLLM,float16,128 output cap and actual latency/response lengths support equal .071s/21-token response to base, with training hardware/epochs disclosed. Full SOP/DOM/BERT preprocessing/input/pipeline cost and repetitions absent; .123/.071≈1.73 contradicts10x, preventing stronger general practical no-cost claim.
search_scope: Section4.2 Implementation Details and Computation Cost; Table5 response-only length definition

reason: Method/results/appendix operation and SOP tables plus supplied figures are available. Missing full schema image is localized and nonessential to numeric score interpretation; deployment ambiguity is an author-description conflict retained in claim_support, not falsely classified as no fulltext or proven leakage.
readable_rationale: The specific action/interaction formats and SOP training idea address plausible mobile workflow problems, with useful same-backbone plan/state controls. Evidence remains offline, and the named task-completion metric is an action-fraction average. A1.49pp improvement is modest and lacks test-denominator/variance isolation; critical SOP input availability is ambiguous. Equal reported short-response timing is credible within Table5, but its tenfold prose is arithmetically false and total practical cost/privacy benefits remain unproven.
